s1.syndrome_frame: Widespread skin condition with progressive worsening and characteristic plaques
salient_findings: Widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale
key_facts: The skin condition has progressively worsened
The condition involves 90% of her body surface area (BSA)
Polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques are present on the trunk and extremities
The plaques involve 30% of the body surface area (BSA)
Eyebrow hairs are sparse and less than 5 mm long
Scalp hairs are coarse and brittle
Skin biopsy showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis
Trichography showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Characteristic polycyclic serpiginous erythematous plaques and progressive worsening

shortlist.label: Psoriasis vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy showing psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis

shortlist.label: Erythroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Widespread skin condition involving 90% of body surface area

shortlist.label: Ichthyosiform dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Coarse and brittle scalp hairs and sparse eyebrow hairs

shortlist.label: Exfoliative dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive worsening and involvement of large body surface area

raw.rationale: The combination of psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis on skin biopsy, trichography showing nodal swelling with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end, and the specific hair findings (sparse eyebrow hairs and coarse brittle scalp hairs) are characteristic of Netherton syndrome.

rejected.label: psoriasis
rejected.why: While the skin biopsy shows psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia, the specific hair findings and trichography results are not typical for psoriasis

rejected.label: pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not align with the characteristic features of pityriasis rubra pilaris

rejected.label: atopic dermatitis
rejected.why: The presence of psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia and specific hair abnormalities are not characteristic of atopic dermatitis

rejected.label: lichen sclerosus et atrophicus
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not match the typical features of lichen sclerosus et atrophicus
